guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our disagreement with the market is not based on Purdue having a favorable defensive matchup. We see Notre Dame holding clear efficiency advantages on the ground, through the air and in creating scoring opportunities. The market is asking whether those advantages produce sustained separation; our numbers are slightly less aggressive on that point because we see Purdue having enough offensive capability to offer resistance.

Purdue’s opener provides some context without settling the question. The offense generated 523 yards, while Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns. We are not treating production against Indiana State as proof that it carries over against Notre Dame, especially with 16 players making their first Purdue starts and 38 making their Purdue debuts. Browne’s experience and the encouraging opening performance help explain our lean toward Purdue, but the defensive matchup leaves us without enough value to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Notre Dame’s rushing offense against Purdue’s run defense. Our efficiency numbers identify this as a major advantage for Notre Dame, and it connects directly to the Irish’s ability to generate repeated scoring opportunities. Purdue allowed only 66 rushing yards in its opener, but we do not view one result against Indiana State as evidence that the larger concern has disappeared. If Purdue cannot limit efficient early-down rushing, the separation risk that keeps us cautious becomes much more significant.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State.
Purdue produced 523 yards of total offense against Indiana State, its first 500-yard game since Oct. 12, 2024 at Illinois.
Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State.
Fame Ijeboi led Purdue with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and added two receptions for 30 yards.
FAU transfer Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut.
Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.
Sixteen players made their first Purdue starts and 38 players made their Purdue debuts in the season opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue is scheduled to host Notre Dame at Ross-Ade Stadium on Sept. 26, 2026; Notre Dame was ranked No. 4 in this guide.
Purdue lost 56-30 to Notre Dame in 2025, Barry Odom's only previous game against Notre Dame as Purdue's head coach.
Against Notre Dame in 2025, Devin Mockobee took a handoff and threw a return pass to Ryan Browne for a 14-yard touchdown reception.

quarterback.fact: Ryan Browne is Purdue's returning starting quarterback and has started 15 career games for the Boilermakers.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and threw for 2,153 yards and nine touchdowns.
Browne's 317-yard performance against Indiana State was his fourth career 300-yard passing game.
Browne spent the spring of 2025 at North Carolina before transferring back to Purdue during the spring portal window.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed for the backup quarterback position during the spring and summer.

offensive_personnel.fact: Minnesota transfer Fame Ijeboi is part of a reworked backfield following the graduation of Devin Mockobee, who led Purdue in rushing four times and finished with 2,987 career rushing yards.
Antonio Harris is the lone returning running back; he rushed for 305 yards and two touchdowns on 69 carries in 2025.
Running back Travis Terrell Jr. transferred from Jackson State after rushing for 1,067 yards and nine touchdowns over two seasons.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned after missing the 2025 season with injuries.
Purdue added receivers Xavier Townsend from Iowa State, Asaad Waseem from FAU and Bisi Owens from Penn through the transfer portal.
True freshman Brock Brownfield became the first true freshman to start on Purdue's offensive line in a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona was the only returning offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey played in 11 games.
Purdue added five offensive-line transfers, including Boaz Stanley with 21 previous starts, Nuku Mafi with 12 and Micah Banuelos with five.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Charles Correa returned after recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks in 12 starts during 2025.
Purdue added defensive linemen Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought a combined 81 games of college experience.
Defensive end transfers Elo Modozie and Keyshawn Burgos entered 2026 with 7.5 and 2.5 career sacks, respectively.
Transfer linebacker Jojo Hayden started his Purdue debut against Indiana State and recorded four tackles and one tackle for loss.
Transfer defensive back Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup against Indiana State.
Transfer defensive back Don Saunders recorded three tackles, one-half tackle for loss and a 35-yard interception-return touchdown in his Purdue debut.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to assistant head coach and running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach.
Zach Crabtree joined Purdue as offensive line coach after serving in that role at Fresno State in 2025.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and is expected to miss the 2026 season.
Tight end George Burhenn returned against Indiana State for his first game action in 349 days and caught two passes for 43 yards.
Burhenn's 2025 season ended when he was injured at Notre Dame after catching nine passes for 94 yards in four games.
Chauncey Magwood returned after missing most of 2025 with an injury and caught a six-yard touchdown against Indiana State.
Defensive lineman TJ Lindsey returned after an injury limited him to three games in 2025.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue rushed for 177 yards and passed for 346 yards in its season opener.
Purdue did not commit a turnover against Indiana State.
Five different Purdue players scored touchdowns against Indiana State, and each recorded his first points as a Boilermaker.
Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen to its 2026 roster, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue allowed Indiana State 284 total yards, including 66 rushing yards and 218 passing yards.
Purdue recorded three sacks and eight tackles for loss against Indiana State.
Indiana State recorded 12 first downs against Purdue.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts and all five extra-point attempts against Indiana State, with a long field goal of 39 yards.
Echeverria Lozano's three field goals were the most by a Purdue true freshman in a game since at least 1995.
Buffalo transfer Dylan Drennan punted once for 54 yards with a 49-yard net in his Purdue debut.
Xavier Townsend returned three punts for 24 yards against Indiana State.

series_context.fact: Notre Dame leads the Purdue series 61-26-2 and has won 10 consecutive meetings.
The Sept. 26 Purdue-Notre Dame game is played for the Shillelagh Trophy.

other_relevant.fact: Barry Odom is in his second season as Purdue's head coach and entered the Wake Forest week with a 3-10 record at Purdue.

Quarterback Ryan Browne, linebacker Charles Correa, defensive back Hudauri Hines, offensive lineman Jude McCoskey, wide receiver De'Nylon Morrissette and defensive lineman Curt Neal were named Purdue's 2026 captains.
